introHtml:
Harbour Tank Co handles oil tank replacement in St. John's and the surrounding Avalon communities. We pull the old tank, set the new one, connect it to your furnace, and have a licensed inspector tag and register it so your fuel company can deliver again. The price is $3,200 for a 200-gallon steel tank or $3,850 for fibreglass, and both include removal of the old tank.

Call (709) 800-3117 and we'll get you a written estimate and a swap date, or read on to see how the process works and what drives the cost.

sections.heading: How to tell if your oil tank needs replacing
sections.html:
Every registered oil tank in Newfoundland and Labrador carries a small metal HOST tag near the fill or the outlet. Stamped on it is an expiry in MM-YYYY form. If that month has passed, the tank is expired in the eyes of the province and of your fuel supplier, no matter how solid it looks.

The expiry comes from the Heating Oil Storage Tank System Regulations, NLR 60/03. Section 15 sets a life of 10 to 25 years for mild-steel tanks depending on where it sits, how thick the steel is, and where the outlet is. An outdoor single-wall 14-gauge tank with an end outlet, which is the most common setup on older St. John's homes, gets 10 years. Indoor tanks, thicker steel and bottom outlets earn longer terms.

Beyond the tag, watch for these signs:

  • Rust blistering or flaking on the bottom seam or the legs
  • A wet or dark patch on the ground or floor under the tank
  • Oil smell near the tank or in the basement
  • Legs sinking, tilting or sitting on cracked pads
  • A fill or vent pipe that's rusted through at the threads

Any of those on their own is worth a call. A tank that's both expired and showing rust is a same-day conversation, especially in winter.

sections.heading: What oil tank replacement costs in St. John's
sections.html:
We keep pricing simple. A 200-gallon steel tank, installed, with the old tank removed and hauled away, is $3,200. A fibreglass tank of the same size is $3,850, again with removal included. Both prices are in Canadian dollars and cover the tank, stand, fittings, fill and vent piping, connection to your furnace line, and the inspector's tagging and registration visit.

The difference between the two comes down to lifespan. Steel goes back on the 10 to 25 year clock under NLR 60/03 the day it's installed. Fibreglass isn't subject to that same expiry table, so it's the tank we suggest for anyone planning to stay put or thinking about resale. Read more on our fibreglass upgrade page.

Extras that can change the number are rare but real: a tank that has to be cut up to get out of a tight basement, a new concrete pad because the old one has heaved, or a long run of new copper line. We'll flag any of those in the written estimate, not after the truck shows up. For a fuller breakdown see our cost guide.

sections.heading: What happens on swap day
sections.html:
Here's the day, start to finish, so you know what to expect.

  • Site check. We confirm the tank location, look at the stand and pad, and check the furnace line and shut-off.
  • Drain and disconnect. Any oil left in the old tank is pumped out and saved where it's clean enough to reuse. Lines are capped so nothing drips.
  • Remove the old tank. It goes on the truck for proper disposal. If you'd rather handle removal separately, see oil tank removal.
  • Set and connect the new tank. New stand, new fittings, new fill and vent, and a fresh filter on the furnace line. We bleed the line and fire the furnace to make sure it runs.
  • Tag and register. A licensed inspector tags the new system and registers it with the province. You get the confirmation of registration for your insurer and, if you're selling, your real estate lawyer.

Most swaps are done in a single visit. Once the new HOST tag is on, call your fuel company and book a delivery. The driver will see a current date and fill you without a fuss.

sections.heading: Where we replace oil tanks
sections.html:
We're based in St. John's and work across the Northeast Avalon and out into Conception Bay South and Conception Bay North. That includes Mount Pearl, Paradise, Conception Bay South, Torbay, Portugal Cove-St. Philip's and Bay Roberts.

Older neighbourhoods in the city centre, the Goulds, Kilbride and Shea Heights tend to have the most 10-year outdoor steel tanks coming due, but we see plenty of expired tags in newer subdivisions too. If your community isn't listed, call anyway. If it's on the Avalon, we can likely get to you.

Not sure whether your tank is due? Send a photo of the HOST tag to info@harbourtank.ca or call (709) 800-3117 and we'll read the date for you.

faq.q: How long does a steel oil tank last in Newfoundland?
faq.a: Under NLR 60/03 section 15, a mild-steel tank is allowed 10 to 25 years depending on gauge, outlet position and whether it's indoors or out. The most common tank on an older St. John's home, an outdoor single-wall 14-gauge tank with an end outlet, gets 10 years. The exact expiry for your tank is stamped on the HOST tag as MM-YYYY.

faq.q: My fuel company refused to deliver. What do I do?
faq.a: Section 13 of the regulations says a supplier can't legally deliver to an unregistered or expired tank, so the driver had no choice. Call us at (709) 800-3117 and we'll book a swap, usually within the week, and faster if you're out of oil. A new 200-gallon steel tank is $3,200 installed and once the inspector tags it you can rebook your delivery. Our expired tank emergency page walks through the steps.

faq.q: Should I go with steel or fibreglass?
faq.a: Steel is $3,200 installed and goes back on the 10 to 25 year expiry clock. Fibreglass is $3,850, won't rust, and isn't tied to the same steel expiry table under NLR 60/03. If you plan to stay in the house more than 10 years or want a clean answer for a buyer's lawyer, the extra $650 for fibreglass usually pays for itself.

faq.q: How long does the replacement take?
faq.a: Most swaps are finished in one visit of about four to six hours, including draining the old tank, setting the new one, and firing the furnace. Booking is typically same-week from the day you approve the written estimate. The inspector's tagging and registration visit is coordinated so you're not waiting on paperwork to get oil.

faq.q: Will I get paperwork for my insurance company or lawyer?
faq.a: Yes. The licensed inspector who tags the new tank registers it with the province and issues a confirmation of registration. Insurers ask for it at renewal and real estate lawyers ask for it before closing. Keep a copy with your house papers and take a photo of the HOST tag so the expiry date is easy to find later.
